note: The comparison's ITEM TABLE, fixed in the Harness (kogaki#872).
WHICH PACKET INFORMATION MUST BE RECOVERABLE IS DECIDED ONCE, HERE, per
item class — and the judging model never assigns one. It answers one
question about one pair and returns one of three tokens. src/review-draft.mjs
READS this file rather than restating it, the same arrangement
src/recovered-schema.json has with the recovery half: amending the table is
one edit and never a two-copy divergence.
`class` IS THE CONSEQUENCE, not a severity. A Step is sent to correction only
on a `fails` in a PRESERVED item; a best-effort fail rides along when that
Step is re-realized anyway. There is no score, no ranking and no aggregate —
the three tokens are the whole vocabulary, and `cannot-decide` is never
rounded to either neighbour.
`mode` IS WHO DECIDES, and it is the half that keeps the model out of the
mechanical items:
- `mechanical` — the Harness decides from string facts about the Draft and
the Packet. NO join Packet is rendered and no model call is made.
- `judged`     — the Harness renders one join Packet (the declared line,
the recovered line, the quoted span, one question) and records the
verdict that comes back.
- `paired`     — the Harness pairs the recovered entries against the
declared ones MECHANICALLY; an entry that pairs with nothing is decided
here, by name, with no model call, and the paired set is then judged.
This is the one hybrid, and it exists because `widened` is a fact about
the pairing rather than a reading of it.
`declared_block` names the Packet block the declared side is read from, and
src/review-draft.mjs refuses BY NAME when a Packet carries no such block —
a missing block is a PACKET GAP filed against src/packet-template.md, per
the owner's 2026-09-04 closed-input ruling, and never something the
comparison works around.
`recovered_field` names the field of src/recovered-schema.json the recovered
side is read from. `null` means the recovered side IS THE PROSE — the
negative items, which assert that something is absent from the passage.
NOT COMPARED, enumerated so a reader can tell a boundary from a hole:
rationale, materials, reader_state_before, and the thesis and reader target
per Step. The article level is the cold reader's (kogaki#873).
THE PACKET'S SHAPE IS DATA, not a literal in the runtime (kogaki#872).
src/review-draft.mjs reads a declared block by its KIND, and every label,
heading and fixed instruction sentence the reader keys on lives here. Two
things follow, and the second is the reason:
- amending src/packet-template.md is one edit here and never a hunt
through the comparison for a string that used to match;
- the runtime carries no literal that HAPPENS to equal a field name
somewhere else. `grounds`, `purpose` and `reader_state_after` are
each a Packet label AND an item id AND (for two of them) a recovered
record field, and a runtime spelling them out cannot be told apart
from one restating the table or the schema. A synonym in a join key
is the same defect as a divergence.
`after_words` is the template's own fixed instruction paragraph, matched
as a WORD SEQUENCE so a rewrap — which changes nothing — does not silently
hand the instruction back as the block's value.

move_excerpt.heading: An exemplar of this Move — FORM ONLY
move_excerpt.after_words: Read it for the shape of the movement and nothing else.

section_placement.heading: The Section this Step sits in
section_placement.after_words: one, and the line below says which. Where it continues, the heading is already on the page and you are writing further into it: do not restate the heading's claim, and do not open a new subject.

note: THE SECOND PASS'S BOUND IS DATA, for the reason the packet_blocks
note gives one block down (kogaki#874). `check` re-judges the
corrected Steps' own items, the two CONTINUITY items on the Step
immediately after each correction, and every mechanical item over
the whole Draft -- and the runtime names none of those ids, because
an item id spelled out in the runtime cannot be told from one
restating this table.
`successor_items` is TWO ids and the issue names the properties they
carry: `reader_state_before` continuity and `restates`. The Packet
renders a `reader_state_before` slot and this table declares NO
reader for it -- the block that carries the reader's INCOMING state
is `already_knows`, which is what `already-knows` compares -- so the
continuity item is that one rather than a new item over a block
nothing reads. Both are best-effort, which is the qualifier the
issue's own sentence carries.
`restates-earlier-step` is ALSO mechanical, so it is in the bound
twice over: once for every Step and once as a successor item. That
is not redundancy to remove -- it is the item whose INPUT a
correction changes, since its haystack is the earlier prose, and
listing it here says why the successor is re-checked at all.
`drift_blocks` are the Packet blocks the drift measure reports
verbatim overlap against -- the ground and state lines. Same
arrangement, same reason.
Thresholds are INPUTS TO THE HARNESS AND NEVER OUTPUT. No emitted line
carries one — a comparison line renders line numbers and nothing else
numeric, so a reader cannot mistake a tuning constant for evidence.

items.unpaired_sentence: this recovered claim pairs with no ground the Packet declares, so the passage asserts more than it was given — widened
items.question: Does this recovered claim assert no more than the ground it is paired with? Answer `fails` if the claim goes beyond the ground in scope, in certainty, or in subject.
Do the declared reader state and the recovered one describe the same reader? Answer `fails` if a reader in the recovered state would not be in the declared one.

Is every term the Packet says to introduce here actually introduced in this passage — usable by the reader afterwards? Answer `fails` if a declared term is used without being made usable, or is not present at all.
Read the Move's constraints and failure_modes against the shape recovered from the prose. Answer `fails` if a constraint is violated or a failure mode fired.

when_declared_absent.sentence: this Move record carries no exemplar, so no subject matter could leak from one

items.question: The exemplar was FORM ONLY. Does any entity, fact, claim or term from it appear in this passage? Answer `fails` if it does — this item asks about the exemplar's subject matter, never its shape.
Is any ground carried more weakly in the prose than the Packet declares it, with no concession recovered for it? Answer `fails` if a ground was softened silently.
Do the declared purpose and the recovered one name the same job for this Step? Answer `fails` if the passage is doing a different job.
Does the passage re-introduce a term the reader already knows — explaining again what an earlier Step established? Answer `fails` if it does.

The Packet says whether this Step opens its Section or continues one. Where it CONTINUES, does the passage re-open the subject or restate the heading's claim? Answer `fails` if it does; answer `holds` where the Step opens its Section, since the item does not bind there.
Read the passage against the three register tests the Packet states, cited as its clauses. Answer `fails` if one of them is not met, naming which.
